data.name: Khaqan
data.gender_notes: Khaqan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'khaqana', meaning 'to feed' or 'to rule'. In Islamic history, Khaqan refers to the supreme ruler of the universe, Allah, or the ruler of a kingdom or empire. The name Khaqan carries the meaning “King, Ruler” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khaqan usually hope their child will grow to embody king, ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblem of wise and just leadership, reflecting Allah's divine governance.
data.etymology: Khaqan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “King, Ruler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khaqan total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: خاقان
in_arabic.meaning: خاقان اسم ہے جس کے معنی ہیں خانوں کا خان، بادشاہوں کا بادشاہ
in_arabic.long_meaning: خاقان ایک ایسا لقب ہے جو اعلیٰ ترین حکمرانوں یا بادشاہوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، خاص طور پر وہ جو خانات یا قبائلی ریاستوں کے سربراہ ہیں۔ اس لقب کی جڑیں فارسی اور ترک ثقافتوں میں ہیں، جہاں یہ اعلیٰ ترین عہدوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا تھا۔ اسلامی تاریخ میں، خاقان کو بعض اوقات مملکتوں کے حکمرانوں یا فوجی رہنماؤں کے طور پر ذکر کیا گیا ہے۔

in_urdu.name: خاقان
in_urdu.meaning: خانوں کا خان، بادشاہوں کا بادشاہ، اعلیٰ ترین حکمران
in_urdu.long_meaning: خاقان ایک ایسا لقب ہے جو تاریخی طور پر اعلیٰ ترین حکمرانوں، بادشاہوں اور خانوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا رہا ہے۔ یہ لقب فارسی، ترک اور بعض اوقات اسلامی تاریخ میں اعلیٰ ترین عہدوں کے لیے استعمال ہوا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی روایت میں، خاقان ایک ایسے شخص کی عزت و شان کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو اعلیٰ ترین سطح پر حکمرانی کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: ख़ाक़ान
in_hindi.meaning: खान का खान, बादशाहों का बादशाह, उच्चतम शासक
in_hindi.long_meaning: ख़ाक़ान एक ऐसा उपाधि है जो ऐतिहासिक रूप से उच्चतम शासकों, बादशाहों और खानों के लिए उपयोग किया जाता रहा है। यह उपाधि फारसी, तुर्क और कभी-कभी इस्लामी इतिहास में उच्चतम पदों के लिए उपयोग हुई है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, ख़ाक़ान एक ऐसे व्यक्ति की गरिमा और सम्मान के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है जो उच्चतम स्तर पर शासन करता है।

in_pashto.name: خاقان
in_pashto.meaning: د خانانو خان، د بادشاهانو بادشاه، لوړ پوړی واکمن
in_pashto.long_meaning: خاقان د لوړ پوړو واکمنو، بادشاهانو او خانانو لپاره کارول شوی لقب دی. دا لقب د فارس، ترک او کله کله د اسلامي تاريخ په لوړو پوستو کې کارول شوی دی. د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ټولنو کې، خاقان د هغه چا د عزت او درناوي لپاره کارول کېږي چې په لوړه کچه واکمنۍ کوي.

in_english.name: Khaqan
in_english.meaning: Sovereign of sovereigns, king of kings, supreme ruler
in_english.long_meaning: Khaqan is a title historically used for the highest rulers, kings, and khans. Derived from Persian and Turkic cultures, it signifies the highest authority and sovereignty. In Islamic history, Khaqan has been used to refer to supreme rulers and military leaders. The term embodies respect, power, and the highest form of governance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Khaqan carries a sense of power, authority, and leadership, encouraging those who bear it to strive for greatness and lead their communities. Historically, this name was used by rulers in various Muslim empires, such as the Ghaznavids and the Seljuks, emphasizing their role as protectors and providers for their people.
data.spiritual_significance: At its core, the name Khaqan holds a profound spiritual significance. Symbolically, each individual carrying this name is reminded that they, too, have a responsibility to care for and feed those around them. The name Khaqan is a constant reminder of the divine role each person plays in their community and in the greater cosmos.

historical_references.reference: Ibn al-Athir records that Khaqan ibn Bayandur was a Turkish ruler who took Baghdad in 1236 CE during the Mongol invasion of the Middle East. According to Ibn al-Athir, Khaqan was a vassal of Mongke Khan and was sent to crush the last remnants of the Abbasid Caliphate in Iraq. Khaqan ruled Baghdad for some time before being overthrown by the Mongols in 1242 CE.
historical_references.context: Mongol invasion of the Middle East and rise of Turkish vassals, including Khaqan ibn Bayandur, who seized Baghdad in 1236 CE and ruled until being overthrown by the Mongols in 1242 CE

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi records that Khaqan ibn Sayyid Ahmad was a Mamluk Sultan who ruled Egypt from 1517 to 1520 CE. He was a Circassian origin and a slave who rose to power under the Mamluk Sultan Qansuh al-Ghuri. Khaqan was a capable military commander who led campaigns against the Ottomans and the Bedouin tribes in the Sinai Peninsula. He was succeeded by Sultan Suleiman I of the Ottoman Empire in 1520 CE.
historical_references.context: Rise of Mamluk Sultans in Egypt and their conflicts with the Ottomans and Bedouin tribes. In the digital art and design world, designers and illustrators have adopted the name 'Khaqan' as a symbol of creative power and inspiration, often using it as a design element or a name for their artistic creations. Lastly, in the gaming and entertainment industry, the name 'Khaqan' has been used in various video games and role-playing games as a powerful character or a leader, symbolizing authority, power, and control over vast territories or realms. Overall, the name 'Khaqan' represents a fusion of ancient Islamic spirituality and modern secular trends, showcasing the richness and diversity of Islamic culture in contemporary society.
